2. The brief facts of the case as per claim petition are that on 12.01.2016, Vijay (deceased herein),
who was working as a Supervisor in Miglani Tempo Transport Company, Shahdara, Delhi, was going from Village Milana to Baraut on a motorcycle being driven by his friend Vikrant and at about 06.00 p.m., when they reached in front of Gayatri Devi College, Chhaprauli Road, P.S. Baraut,
Baghpat, U.P., all of a sudden the driver of a JCB vehicle bearing no. UP-17T-8434 (in short 'offending vehicle') turned it without following the traffic rules and without taking necessary precautions, due to which its Bokit bumped into the head of the deceased with great force.
As a result of the impact, the deceased fell down on the road and sustained injuries.

The deceased was taken to Astha Hospital, Baraut, from where he was referred to KMC Hospital, Baghpat Road,
Meerut, U.P. where he expired during the course of his treatment on 17.01.2016.
______________________________________________________________________ 3.
In connection with the accident, FIR no.91/2016, under sections 279/338/304-A IPC was registered at PS Baraut, U.P.

During investigation, it was found out that at the time of the accident,
the offending vehicle was being driven by respondent no.3, owned by respondent no.2 and insured with respondent no.1.

After completion of the investigation, charge-sheet under the aforesaid offences against the respondent no.1 was filed before the concerned court and the present claim petition seeking compensation was filed before this Tribunal.
4. Respondent no.1/ insurance company filed its written statement.

Apart from taking general objections, it is contended that the FIR was lodged on 02.02.2016 i.e.
after a lapse of 21 days from the date of occurrence of alleged accident (12.01.2016).

It is also stated that, as per site plan, the motorcycle on which the deceased was travelling as a pillion rider was being driven on the wrong side of the road and the accident occurred due to negligence of the driver of the motorcycle, namely, Vikrant S/o Ratan Singh and
therefore, said Vikrant and the insurer of the said motorcycle are necessary parties to the present claim petition.

It is further contended that,
as the petitioners have not filed any document in support of their averment that the deceased was working as a supervisor, which indicated that the deceased was unemployed at the time of the accident.
It is also contended that the liability of the offending vehicle is vicarious and subject to proof that the driver of the offending vehicle was rashly and negligently driving the same.

______________________________________________________________________ 5. Respondents no.2 and 3 filed their common written statement stating that respondent no.2 was the owner of the alleged offending vehicle and respondent no.3 was the driver.
It is stated that the vehicle no. UP-17T-8434 (JCB) was insured with the respondent no.3/ Oriental Insurance Company Ltd.
Both the respondents have denied the occurrence of the accident as alleged and also denied all other averments made by the petitioners in their claim petition.

9. I have heard the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the parties and perused the evidence and other materials placed on record.

Whether respondent no.3/ driver was driving the offending vehicle no.
UP-17T-8434 on 12.01.2016 at about 6.00 P.M. in front of Gayatri Devi College,
Chhaprauli Road, Baraut, U.P within the jurisdiction of PS Baraut in a rash and negligent manner and caused the death of deceased Vijay? OPP 10.
It is settled law that, in an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
A holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.

Reference may be made to the judgments titled as 'New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v. Sakshi Bhutani & Others', MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012, 'Bimla Devi & Others v.
Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others' (2009) 13 SC 530, 'Parmeshwari v. Amirchand &
Others' 2011 (1) SCR 1096 & 'Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Others', 2018, Law Suit (SC) 303.

Assessment of Income of the deceased 26.
PW1 i.e., the father of the deceased deposed that his deceased son was working as Supervisor in Miglani Tempo Transport Company, Shahdara, Delhi and getting Rs.15,000/- per month as salary.

As the petitioners have not placed any other document on record to show the income of deceased as claimed, in the absence of any documentary evidence of income of the deceased, his income has to be assessed at par with minimum wages applicable to non- matriculate category of workers prevalent in U.P. on the date of accident (12.01.2016), which may be considered equivalent to semi- skilled category.
At the relevant time, the minimum wages applicable to semi-skilled category of workers in U.P. were Rs.7,497/- per month.
Thus, the income of the deceased is considered to be Rs.7,497/-per month.

sentences.text: In this case, the parents are the only petitioners.

The deceased was 21 years old at the time of accident and it has nowhere been stated in the petition or in the evidence of PW1 (father of the deceased) that the deceased was married at the time of accident.

With respect to deductions towards personal living expenses of a bachelor, the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Pranay Sethi &
Others (Supra) laid down the guiding principle as under:
"31. Where the deceased was a bachelor and the claimants are the parents, the deduction follows a different principle.
In regard to bachelors, normally 50% is deducted as personal and living expenses, because it is assumed that a bachelor would tend to spend more on himself.

Even otherwise, there is also the possibility of his getting married in a short time, in which event the contribution to the parent(s)
and siblings is likely to be cut drastically.

Further, subject to evidence to the contrary,
the father is likely to have his own income and will not be considered as a dependent and the mother alone will be considered as a dependent.

In the absence of evidence to the contrary, brothers and sisters will not be considered as dependents, because they will either be independent and earning, or married, or be dependent on the father."
______________________________________________________________________ 30.
Therefore, in this case, 50% of the income of the deceased is to be deducted towards his personal living expenses.

Loss of Dependency:
31. sentences.text: NON-PECUNIARY DAMAGES 32.

In the light of the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court, dated 31.10.2017, in case of Pranay Sethi & Others (Supra), a compensation of Rs.40,000/-, 15,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively has been fixed on account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses and further, it is required to be enhanced @ 10% in every three years.
The accident of the deceased in this case occurred on 12.01.2016 and he succumbed to injuries on 17.01.2016.

Therefore, a compensation of Rs.40,000/-,
Rs.15,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively on account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses is required to be granted.

Further, in view of the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case titled as United India Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur & Ors., Civil Appeal no. 2705 of 2020, decided on 30.06.2020, claimants are required to be granted spousal c o n s o r t i u m ,

sentences.text: Now, the question arises as to which of the respondents is liable to pay the compensation amount.
Admittedly, the insurance company has contractual and statutory liability to indemnify the insured.
The respondent insurance company has also admitted that the offending vehicle was duly insured.

Though learned counsel for the insurance company has taken the defence that the driver of the motorcycle in which the deceased was travelling was moving in the wrong direction but the said fact could not be proved during the enquiry proceedings and no evidence has been led to prove the same.
It is not disputed that the respondent no.3/ driver was having a valid driving license to drive the offending vehicle.
Therefore, the respondent no.1/ insurance company is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.

This Tribunal awards a compensation of Rs.12,48,000/- (Rs. Twelve Lakhs Forty-Eight Thousand Only) along with interest @ 7% per annum from the date of filing of this claim petition till realization in favour of the petitioners to be paid by the respondent no.1/ insurance company.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is settled law that, in an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
A holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.
Reference may be made to the judgments titled as 'New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v. Sakshi Bhutani & Others', MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012, 'Bimla Devi & Others v.
Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others' (2009) 13 SC 530, 'Parmeshwari v. Amirchand &
Others' 2011 (1) SCR 1096 & 'Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Others', 2018, Law Suit (SC) 303.

Thus, an adverse inference is liable to be drawn against him to the effect that the accident in question occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by him in view of the law laid down in case of Cholamandalam M.S. General Insurance Company Ltd. v. Kamlesh,
